allowed_claims: EU isolation is enabled by default for every Fathom customer, with nothing to set up.
No changes to the embed script are needed to use EU isolation.
Fathom automatically routes data from EU visitors to be processed in the EU, and data from all other visitors to be processed in the US.
EU isolation treats visitors from Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom as EU for data-routing purposes, even though they are non-EU member nations.
Fathom's EU servers are located in Falkenstein, Helsinki, and Nuremberg.
Extreme EU Isolation routes all global traffic through the EU by using the script URL https://cdn-eu.usefathom.com/script.js instead of the default embed script.
Firewall settings are adjusted by going to Settings, then Sites, clicking the site, then clicking the Firewall tab.
The site firewall offers six list tabs to configure: Pages, IPs, Referrers, Domains, Countries, and Events.
Blocking pages, IPs, domains, or countries in the firewall does not restrict visitor access to the site; it only prevents those visits from appearing in the Fathom dashboard.
Page blocking supports wildcards, such as /about/*, to block all pages under a given path (e.g. /about/team, /about/luna).
IP blocking supports wildcard patterns, e.g. 100.100.100.* blocks any IP starting with 100.100.100., such as 100.100.100.1 and 100.100.100.123.
Only IPv4 addresses are currently supported for wildcard IP blocking.
Blocking a country in the firewall keeps that country's visitors able to view the website while excluding their pageviews and analytics data from showing up in Fathom.
Referrer blocking supports wildcards, e.g. *.example.com blocks all subdomains of example.com as referrers.
Once one or more allowed domains are added to the Domains firewall list, data coming from any other domain is blocked instantly.
Wildcard domain entries like *.example.com in the allowed domains list cover subdomains (e.g. subdomain.example.com, www.example.com) but do not allow the root domain example.com itself.
The Events firewall tab can drop junk/unwanted event names at collect time, or restrict collection to only the names sent on purpose.

In the Events firewall, Block mode drops the listed event names while still collecting every other event; Allow mode collects only the listed names/wildcard patterns, and an empty allow list collects every event.
For dynamic event names (for example Shopify product titles), an Events allow list needs a wildcard such as 'Product *'; a tight allow list of exact names will drop those dynamic events.
The firewall only stops future visits; existing spam already in reports must be cleaned up using Data removals in the site's Manage settings.
Fathom's tracking script can be installed via Fathom's WordPress plugin or one of Fathom's other integrations, placed in the header of the site's code.
Fathom's dashboard is live and real-time, so script installation can be verified by checking whether a visit shows up in the 'Realtime' count at the top of the dashboard.
Fathom provides a browser console command, fathom.blockTrackingForMe(), that blocks tracking for the current browser on a page where Fathom is installed.
The blockTrackingForMe setting is stored in the browser's local storage, so it continues working for future visits from that browser.
Fathom's embed script is a single script tag, <script src="https://cdn.usefathom.com/script.js" data-site="ABCDEFG" defer></script>, with the Site ID as the data-site attribute.
The Site ID is a short, unique code that identifies the site, needed for the tracking snippet, integrations, and API calls.
Fathom's advanced script settings support ignoring canonicals, honouring DNT (Do Not Track), and single-page applications (SPAs), among other options.
EU visitors' personal data stays in the EU while Fathom's anonymized analytics are stored on its US infrastructure.
Fathom customers do not need to show cookie notices.
Fathom's EU Cloud is monitored 24/7, is highly available and multi-region, and is available to all customers on all plans.
Every Fathom plan, including the smallest, includes Data Isolation, enabled by default.
Fathom's Data Isolation method works by intelligently routing visitors to the right place to process their data.

For visitors inside the EU, Fathom's CDN routes the pageview to European servers that strip the IP address before it reaches US infrastructure, and the resulting anonymous data is stored on US servers with zero personal data attached.
Fathom can import supported Google Analytics 4 data into the Fathom dashboard.
Fathom does not charge extra for historical GA4 imports.
Fathom's GA4 importer brings in supported daily analytics available through Google's API, but does not recreate every GA4 report or import GA events.
Imported GA4 data has different filtering options from data collected natively by Fathom, and totals can differ between the two tools.
Large GA4 imports may require smaller date ranges.

- Fathom Analytics
